reason: The hypothesis directly restates the 'reactive wear protection' concept from P10, P15, and P16, which already demonstrated in-situ formation of an oxide nanocomposite surface for wear resistance. It applies this same mechanism to a CoCrFeNi matrix, but the core idea, mechanism, and predicted outcome are taken from a single body of work (P10/P15/P16) and combined with the well-known glaze layer concept from P7/P9, without synthesizing disparate findings or proposing a non-trivial new idea.
copied_elements: in-situ formation of adaptive, lubricious oxide nanocomposite (glaze) layer
dense, adherent glaze layer at high temperature
low friction and wear across temperature range
